body: A practical starting point is 2.5 glasses per guest for a full-service reception with a champagne toast and a cocktail hour, split roughly half flutes and half all-purpose wine glasses, plus a 10% breakage and loss allowance. A 200-guest reception therefore lands near 500 pieces, which is a comfortable first order against our carton quantities.

sections.h2: Consolidation saves more than it looks like
body: Mixing categories into one order means one bill of lading, one freight booking and one customs entry rather than three. On a mixed order the customs processing fee is charged once instead of per shipment, and the freight rate improves because a consolidated cube loads better than three partial ones.
Tell us the full list at enquiry stage — the drinkware, the tools, the electrics — and we will quote and consolidate it as one programme.

sections.h2: What is included in every quotation
body: Unit price by volume tier, decoration cost and method, packaging and artwork setup, MOQ per SKU, lead time, carton counts and total cubic volume, payment terms, and the compliance documentation available for the material. If you need pre-shipment inspection, arrange it and we will hold the goods for it.

sections.h2: Terms
body: Payment is 30% deposit with the balance before shipment by bank transfer. FOB dispatch is confirmed per SKU against stock status, quantity and decoration. Quotations are valid for approximately one month.

faqs.q: Is there a minimum order value?
faqs.a: There is no blanket minimum order value. Minimums are set per SKU by carton quantity and, where you want decoration, by the printing minimum for that item.

faqs.q: Can I mix categories in one order?
faqs.a: Yes, and we recommend it. A mixed order ships as one consolidated entry, which reduces freight and customs processing costs compared with splitting the order.

faqs.q: Are the prices on the website final?
faqs.a: No. No price is published on the website. Every unit price is quoted per project against confirmed specification, quantity, decoration, packaging and destination, and the quotation is the only place a firm price appears.

faqs.q: Do you offer samples?
faqs.a: Yes. Sample orders are welcome, and the sample cost is credited against your first bulk order. Samples can be paid by PayPal or credit card, and courier accounts (FedEx, DHL, UPS) can be used for freight.

faqs.q: What payment terms do you accept?
faqs.a: 30% deposit in advance with the balance before shipment, by bank transfer (T/T). PayPal and credit card are accepted for sample and trial orders, and letters of credit are negotiable for container-size programmes. Quotations are valid for approximately one month.

title: Custom Logo Drinkware and Branded Barware | BYF BOOM
intro: Customisation is not a service we add on at the end of a quotation. Colour matching, logo application and retail packaging are planned into the product from the first enquiry, because they change what the item is worth to your buyer.
seoTitle: Custom Logo Drinkware and Branded Barware | BYF BOOM
seoDescription: Custom logo drinkware, Pantone colour matching, laser engraving, electroplating and retail packaging to your specification. Factory direct, proofed before production.

sections.h2: Decoration methods and when to use them
body: Pad printing is the workhorse for drinkware: it holds fine one- and two-colour logos on curved surfaces at a low unit cost, and it is what most event and corporate programmes use. Silk screen suits larger, flatter print areas and heavier ink coverage. Laser engraving cuts into the surface and is the right choice where the mark must not wear off — glassware sold into a hospitality environment, or gifting where the item is expected to last for years. Electroplating is a finish rather than a print: it produces the mirror and metallic looks used on novelty drinkware and premium bar tools, and it can also carry a logo.
For branded bar tools — stoppers, pourers, openers — moulding the logo into the tool itself is possible on high-volume shapes, which removes the print from the wear equation entirely.

sections.h2: Colour matching
body: Send a Pantone reference and we will produce a colour chip or a moulded sample for approval before production starts. Colour is the thing that most often goes wrong in a branded order, and it goes wrong because someone approved a description instead of a sample. A physical approval item removes that risk from the order.

sections.h2: Packaging and retail readiness
body: The same product can be a plain export carton for a corporate giveaway or a printed colour box with a hang tag and UPC barcode for a retail shelf or an online listing. Packaging is quoted as a separate line so you can see exactly what retail readiness costs, and it is priced into the unit cost rather than bolted on at the end.
For gift and promotional programmes, we can also supply the item inside a moulded case or travel box — which is what makes a set of bar tools sellable as a gift rather than as loose components.

sections.h2: What we need from you
body: Vector artwork (AI, EPS or PDF), the Pantone reference for any colour match, the print position and size, the quantity, and the channel the product is going into. That is enough to return a virtual proof and a firm decorated price.

faqs.q: What artwork do you need?
faqs.a: Vector artwork in AI, EPS or PDF. If you only have a bitmap, send it and we will confirm whether it can be redrawn, and what that costs.

faqs.q: Can you match a specific Pantone colour?
faqs.a: Yes. Send the Pantone reference and we will provide a colour chip or moulded sample for approval before production begins.

faqs.q: Which decoration lasts longest?
faqs.a: Laser engraving is the most durable because the mark is cut into the material rather than printed onto it. Pad printing is the most cost-effective for short-run logo programmes.

faqs.q: Can you supply retail packaging and barcodes?
faqs.a: Yes. Printed colour boxes, hang tags, shrink wrap and UPC barcodes are all available, and are quoted as a separate line so the cost is visible.

faqs.a: Why one total quantity is never the whole answer: how the model, colour split, logo versions, accessories, printed packaging and the mould decision each set the workable minimum — and how to plan a first order that stays simple.
